top.title: Argan's Q2 Beat Shows Power Strength as Industrial Margins Stay Soft
top.summary: Argan, Inc. (AGX) reported strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results with earnings up 50.4% and revenue up 61.5%, beating consensus estimates. The Power segment drove margin strength with a 52.9% revenue increase and improved gross margins to 22.4%. However, Industrial revenues doubled but margins fell to 7.3% due to worsening project completion estimates. Management expects Industrial margins to remain below historical norms for another 1-2 quarters.

top.title: AGX Falls 28.1% in a Month as Backlog and Margin Risks Come Into Focus
top.summary: Argan, Inc. (AGX) shares fell 28.1% over a month despite strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results with 61.5% revenue growth and 50.4% earnings increase. The decline reflects investor concerns over backlog contraction from $2.9B to $2.5B, deteriorating margins (gross margin fell to 19.3%, Industrial margin to 7.3%), and unpredictable project award timing. While the company maintains a debt-free balance sheet and strong growth metrics, elevated valuation at 33.1X trailing earnings and execution risks keep the investment case uncertain.

top.title: Is Argan Worth Buying as Growth Surges but Valuation Stays Elevated?
top.summary: Argan Inc. reported 56.5% revenue growth and $126.5 million adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2027's first half, supported by a $2.5 billion backlog. However, the company faces margin pressure with gross margins declining from 25% to 19.3%, and trades at a premium 31.1X forward earnings. While growth signals remain favorable, execution risks and uncertain project timing present challenges to justify the current valuation.

top.title: NX vs. AGX: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
top.summary: A comparison of two Building Products stocks reveals that Quanex Building Products (NX) offers superior value compared to Argan (AGX). top.title: Deadline Alert: Alibaba Group Holding Limited (BABA) Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP About Securities Fraud Lawsuit
top.summary: Alibaba Group Holding Limited faces a class action securities fraud lawsuit covering the period from June 26, 2025 to June 24, 2026. The lawsuit alleges the company failed to disclose its control by or affiliation with China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), which classified it as a Chinese military company under the National Defense Authorization Act. Additionally, Anthropic accused Alibaba of illicitly accessing its Claude AI model through fraudulent accounts. These revelations caused Alibaba's stock to drop approximately 3.9% on June 10, 2026, and an additional 2.7% on June 24, 2026. The deadline to file a lead plaintiff motion is October 5, 2026.

top.title: How Carlyle's Wealth Push Opens New Avenues for Fee Revenue Growth
top.summary: The Carlyle Group is expanding its wealth-management business through strategic acquisitions and partnerships to increase private-market access for advisors and high-net-worth clients. The company acquired MAI Capital Management and Intelliflo, and partnered with SEI and UBS to strengthen its wealth platform. Carlyle targets $2.8 billion in management fees by 2028, up from $2.2 billion in 2025, with wealth and retirement expected to account for 20% of over $200 billion in targeted inflows.

top.title: Ulcerative Colitis Market Outlook: 5 Late-Stage Drug Candidates to Watch | DelveInsight
top.summary: The ulcerative colitis market is experiencing significant growth with emerging therapies addressing unmet needs in moderate-to-severe disease. The market, valued at approximately USD 9.4 billion in 2025, is projected to expand at a CAGR of 7.6% through 2036. Five promising late-stage candidates—Obefazimod (Abivax), Tulisokibart (Merck), Afimkibart (Roche), Icotrokinra (J&J/Protagonist), and Duvakitug (Teva/Sanofi)—are reshaping the treatment landscape with novel mechanisms targeting IL-23 and TL1A pathways, while established biologics and oral therapies continue to maintain market presence.
